subtopic_gates.learner_title: Chemical Symbols, Atomic Notation & Formula Literacy

provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 9 Science Chapter 3 (Atoms and Molecules), Sections 3.2-3.4

technical_core.canonical_statement: An atom is designated by symbol X with atomic number Z (protons) and mass number A (protons + neutrons) as ^A_Z X.
technical_core.why_required: Grounds element identity and atomic composition.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Conflating isotopes or confusing atomic mass with atomic number.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Elementary gases exist as stable diatomic molecules (H2, N2, O2, F2, Cl2, Br2, I2) under standard conditions.
technical_core.why_required: Prevents writing monoatomic elemental gases in chemical equations.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Writing isolated O or H instead of O2 or H2 as chemical reactants.

technical_core.canonical_statement: A subscript denotes the number of bonded atoms in a formula unit; a stoichiometric coefficient denotes the number of distinct formula units.
technical_core.why_required: Prevents catastrophic confusion between substance identity and substance quantity.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Treating 2H as equivalent to H2.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: A mass number, Z atomic number, N neutron count

representations.name: Nuclide Symbol Notation
representations.chemistry_encoded: Top-left mass number, bottom-left atomic number, centered chemical symbol
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Superscript mass number and subscript atomic number placement
representations.common_incorrect_version: Writing mass number as right subscript or confusing with charge
representations.verification_method: Check A >= Z and A - Z equals integer neutron count

model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Nuclear transmutation or mass defect occurs

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify element symbol from periodic authority
Extract proton count Z and calculate neutron count N = A - Z
Distinguish between free elemental atoms and stable diatomic molecules

required_transformations.description: Oxygen gas -> O2(g)
^23_11 Na -> 11 protons, 12 neutrons, 11 electrons

misconceptions.why_plausible: Both contain two hydrogen atoms total
misconceptions.required_counterexample: H2 is stable diatomic gas with covalent bond; 2H represents two separate reactive radical atoms
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Enforce: subscripts modify internal stoichiometry; coefficients scale external quantity

problem_families.name: Nuclide Notation Composition Analysis
problem_families.recognition_cues: Nuclear isotopic symbol with mass and atomic numbers
problem_families.first_technical_move: Read Z for protons and electrons; calculate A - Z for neutrons
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Subtracting atomic number from electron count

problem_families.name: Formula Unit Atom Counting
problem_families.recognition_cues: Chemical formula with parentheses and coefficients
problem_families.first_technical_move: Multiply coefficient by inner subscript and outer parenthetical multiplier
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Adding coefficients instead of multiplying subscripts

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Direct symbolic literacy and integer particle counting

falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Subscripts denote intramolecular bond stoichiometry, coefficients denote quantity of formula units

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Ions, Valency, Polyatomic Radicals & Formal Charge

provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 9 Science Chapter 3, Section 3.4 (What is an Ion?)

technical_core.canonical_statement: An ion is a charged atom or group of atoms formed by the loss of electrons (cation, positive) or gain of electrons (anion, negative).
technical_core.why_required: Establishes physical origin of electrical charge in chemical species.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Believing ions are formed by proton transfer.

technical_core.canonical_statement: A polyatomic ion is a covalently bonded cluster of atoms carrying an overall net charge that acts as a single indivisible chemical unit (e.g. SO4^2-, CO3^2-, NH4+).
technical_core.why_required: Required to prevent decomposing stable radicals during formula writing.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Writing Al2SO43 instead of Al2(SO4)3.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Valency is the combining capacity of an element or radical, corresponding to the number of electrons lost, gained, or shared to achieve a noble gas electron configuration.
technical_core.why_required: Provides predictive capacity for chemical formula construction.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Blind memorization of formulas without valency basis.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: q_ion net charge, Z proton count, N_e electron count, e elementary charge

representations.name: Lewis Charge Bracket Diagram
representations.chemistry_encoded: Element or cluster enclosed in brackets with formal charge indicated as superscript
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Explicit sign and magnitude outside bracket
representations.common_incorrect_version: Writing charge inside brackets or omitting magnitude
representations.verification_method: Check total valence electrons minus formal bonds equals net bracket charge

model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Fractional charges occur only in subatomic quark theory, invalid in chemistry

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify valence shell electron configuration
Determine electrons gained or lost to satisfy octet/duplet rule
Assign signed ionic charge and deduce combining valency

required_transformations.description: Magnesium atom (12p, 10e) -> Mg^2+
Sulfate ion -> SO4^2- with valency 2

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Brackets are optional when writing multiple polyatomic ions (e.g. writing CaOH2 or Al2SO43)
misconceptions.why_plausible: Learner treats the radical as ordinary concatenated letters
misconceptions.required_counterexample: CaOH2 means 1 Ca, 1 O, 2 H; calcium hydroxide requires 2 hydroxide ions Ca(OH)2 (1 Ca, 2 O, 2 H)
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Enforce brackets around polyatomic radical whenever subscript is 2 or greater

problem_families.name: Ion Charge and Valency Determination
problem_families.recognition_cues: Given atomic number or group number, deduce ion formula and valency
problem_families.first_technical_move: Write electron configuration and determine distance to nearest noble gas
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Assigning positive charge to an atom that gains electrons

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Subatomic charge calculation and polyatomic radical bracket rules

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Omitting parentheses around polyatomic ion with subscript > 1
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Polyatomic radicals require brackets when multiplied by stoichiometric subscripts

provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 9 Science Chapter 3, Section 3.4.2 (Writing Chemical Formulae)

technical_core.canonical_statement: In any stable chemical compound, the total positive charge contributed by cations must exactly balance the total negative charge contributed by anions, resulting in net zero charge.
technical_core.why_required: Enforces fundamental physical condition for macroscopic stability.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Tolerating unneutralized ionic formulas such as MgCl or NaSO4.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Chemical formulas are constructed by crossing valencies/charges as opposite subscripts and reducing to simplest integer ratio.
technical_core.why_required: Provides deterministic algorithm for formula generation.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Guessing subscripts or writing unreduced ratios such as Mg2O2.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: n_+ cation count, z_+ cation charge, n_- anion count, z_- anion charge

representations.name: Criss-Cross Valency Diagram
representations.chemistry_encoded: Cation and anion symbols at top, numerical valencies beneath, diagonal crossing lines pointing to subscripts
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Explicit crossing vectors and integer simplification step
representations.common_incorrect_version: Carrying the plus/minus signs into the subscripts (e.g. Mg2+ Cl1- -> Mg-Cl2+)
representations.verification_method: Check total cation charge + total anion charge == 0

model_conditions.condition: Simplest empirical formula unit for ionic lattices
model_conditions.why_needed: Ionic compounds form continuous lattices, not discrete molecules
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Writing NaCl as Na2Cl2 or continuous polymers without stoichiometric justification

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Write symbols of constituent ions with cation first
Write valencies or charge magnitudes below each ion
Criss-cross valencies to form provisional subscripts
Divide by greatest common divisor to simplest integer ratio
Enclose polyatomic radicals in brackets if subscript > 1

required_transformations.description: Magnesium oxide -> Mg^2+, O^2- -> Mg2O2 -> MgO

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Elements combine 1:1 regardless of valency (e.g. magnesium chloride is MgCl)
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Mg loses 2 electrons; each Cl accepts only 1 electron. Therefore 2 Cl ions are required to balance 1 Mg ion: MgCl2
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Enforce net charge electroneutrality check on every proposed formula

problem_families.name: Binary and Polyatomic Formula Construction
problem_families.recognition_cues: Given chemical name of salt or constituent ions, formulate neutral chemical formula
problem_families.first_technical_move: Identify ion charges, write criss-cross valencies, and check for radical brackets
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Leaving unreduced subscripts like Mg2O2 or omitting radical brackets

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Electroneutrality constraints and polyatomic bracket rules

falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Total positive charge must equal total negative charge in stable compound

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Conservation of Mass & Chemical Equation Balancing

provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 10 Science Chapter 1 (Chemical Reactions and Equations), Section 1.1.2

technical_core.canonical_statement: Mass cannot be created or destroyed in a chemical reaction; total mass of reactants must equal total mass of products.
technical_core.why_required: Fundamental governing physical conservation law for chemistry.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Treating unbalanced equations as physically valid representations.

technical_core.canonical_statement: The number of atoms of each element remains strictly conserved before and after a chemical reaction.
technical_core.why_required: Provides the mathematical basis for stoichiometric balancing.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Chemical equations that create or destroy elemental atoms.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Balancing must be achieved exclusively by adjusting integer stoichiometric coefficients in front of formulas; chemical subscripts are strictly immutable.
technical_core.why_required: Altering subscripts mutates the identity of the chemical substance into a different or non-existent compound.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Balancing H2 + O2 by writing H2O2 instead of 2H2O.

mandatory_equations.formula: sum_reactants nu_i * N_{i, k} = sum_products nu_j * N_{j, k}
mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: nu stoichiometric coefficient, N_{i, k} number of atoms of element k in formula unit i

symbols.name: Atom count of element k in species i

representations.name: Atom Inventory Ledger
representations.chemistry_encoded: Three-column ledger: Element Name, Left Hand Side (Reactant) count, Right Hand Side (Product) count
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Explicit counts for all elements and verification that LHS == RHS
representations.common_incorrect_version: Counting atoms without multiplying through by prefix coefficients
representations.verification_method: Check LHS atom count equals RHS atom count for every element in the table

model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Nuclear transmutation requires mass-energy conservation E=mc^2

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Write skeleton equation with verified correct chemical formulas
Compile atom inventory table for all elements
Select element appearing in fewest formulas (usually metal/nonmetal, leaving H and O last)
Insert trial integer coefficient and immediately update inventory
Balance remaining elements (H then O) and verify all counts match

required_transformations.description: Fe + H2O -> Fe3O4 + H2 balanced to 3Fe + 4H2O -> Fe3O4 + 4H2
Hydrogen + Chlorine -> Hydrogen chloride balanced to H2 + Cl2 -> 2HCl

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Subscripts can be changed to make atoms balance (e.g. H2 + O2 -> H2O2 to form water)
misconceptions.required_counterexample: H2O is water; H2O2 is hydrogen peroxide, a completely different toxic bleaching agent
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Strict prohibition: formula subscripts are immutable; balance only with leading coefficients

problem_families.name: Inspection and Algebraic Equation Balancing
problem_families.recognition_cues: Unbalanced skeleton equation requiring lowest whole number integer coefficients
problem_families.first_technical_move: Construct atom inventory table and identify most complex formula unit to anchor
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Changing subscripts within formula units or using fractional coefficients without clearing
problem_families.typical_unknown: Set of lowest whole-number integer coefficients

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: High element interactivity and multi-step linear dependency across coupled equations

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Balancing an equation by mutating a chemical subscript
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Subscripts define substance identity and are strictly immutable during equation balancing

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Physical State Symbols, Precipitation & Gas Evolution

provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 10 Science Chapter 1, Section 1.1.2 (Making Equation More Informative)

technical_core.canonical_statement: Every reactant and product in a complete chemical equation must declare its physical state: solid (s), liquid (l), gas (g), or aqueous solution (aq).
technical_core.why_required: Chemical behavior, enthalpy, and reaction pathway depend critically on aggregation state.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Treating gaseous water (steam) as identical to liquid water.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Liquid (l) denotes a pure liquid substance or solvent; aqueous (aq) denotes a solute dissolved in water, existing as hydrated ions or solvated molecules.
technical_core.why_required: Dissolved ionic compounds behave completely differently from molten or pure liquids.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Writing HCl(l) for hydrochloric acid or NaCl(l) for table salt dissolved in water.

technical_core.canonical_statement: An insoluble solid formed from mixing solutions is a precipitate indicated by (s) or down-arrow; an evolved gas is indicated by (g) or up-arrow.
technical_core.why_required: Ties macroscopic reaction phenomena directly to chemical state.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Failing to recognize precipitate in double displacement reactions.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: BaCl2 aqueous barium chloride, Na2SO4 aqueous sodium sulfate, BaSO4 solid precipitate, NaCl aqueous sodium chloride
mandatory_equations.reference_frame_or_sign: State symbol suffix on every species

representations.name: State-Annotated Chemical Equation
representations.chemistry_encoded: Balanced equation with explicit subscript/suffix state symbols and directional arrows
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: State notation on every chemical participant
representations.common_incorrect_version: Writing naked formulas without state symbols in aqueous reactions
representations.verification_method: Verify solubility rules to confirm precipitate state is (s)

model_conditions.condition: Aqueous solution at 1 atm and 25 deg C
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: High temperature or non-aqueous solvent alters solubility

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify solvent and dissolved status of each participant
Apply solubility rules to determine whether product forms precipitate
Append appropriate state symbol suffix to every participant

required_transformations.description: CaO + H2O -> Ca(OH)2 -> CaO(s) + H2O(l) -> Ca(OH)2(aq)
White precipitate on mixing lead nitrate and potassium iodide -> PbI2(s)

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Aqueous solution and liquid are interchangeable, so HCl(aq) is the same as HCl(l)
misconceptions.why_plausible: Both appear as fluids in a beaker
misconceptions.required_counterexample: HCl(l) is pure liquefied hydrogen chloride at -85 deg C; HCl(aq) is dissolved H+ and Cl- ions in water exhibiting acidic properties
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Strict distinction: (l) is pure liquid; (aq) is water-solvated solution

problem_families.name: State Symbol Assignment and Precipitation Identification
problem_families.recognition_cues: Aqueous double displacement reaction with potential insoluble product
problem_families.first_technical_move: Determine cation-anion exchange pairs and check solubility table
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Labeling soluble salt as solid precipitate or leaving off state symbols

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Distinction between pure phases and solvated aqueous species

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Conflating pure liquid with aqueous solution
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Aqueous species must be distinguished from pure liquid phases

provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 10 Science Chapter 1, Section 1.1.2 & Chapter 2

technical_core.canonical_statement: Reaction arrows declare pathway reversibility: a single forward arrow indicates an irreversible reaction; a double half-arrow indicates dynamic chemical equilibrium.
technical_core.why_required: Distinguishes completion reactions from equilibrium systems.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Treating reversible Haber process or esterification as one-way completion.

technical_core.canonical_statement: External constraints such as temperature (Delta), pressure, light (h*nu), or specific catalysts must be annotated directly above and below the reaction arrow.
technical_core.why_required: Reactions do not proceed without meeting activation and kinetic thresholds.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Presenting high-barrier industrial syntheses as spontaneous room-temperature reactions.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Exothermic reactions release heat (Delta H < 0, heat on product side); endothermic reactions absorb heat (Delta H > 0, heat on reactant side).
technical_core.why_required: Enforces energy conservation and temperature change predictions.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Conflating heat absorption with heat release in decomposition reactions.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: CO2 carbon dioxide, H2O water, C6H12O6 glucose, O2 oxygen; sunlight and chlorophyll are required catalysts/energy sources

representations.name: Reaction Coordinate Diagram
representations.chemistry_encoded: Potential energy vs reaction coordinate showing activation energy barrier and Delta H
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Clear relative energy of products vs reactants and catalyst barrier lowering
representations.common_incorrect_version: Showing exothermic reaction with products higher than reactants
representations.verification_method: Check Delta H = H_products - H_reactants agrees with sign

model_conditions.why_needed: Enthalpy Delta H equals heat exchanged
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Non-constant pressure requires internal energy Delta U analysis

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify if activation energy requires external input (heat, light, catalyst)
Place external energy/catalyst annotations directly across reaction arrow
Assign enthalpy sign Delta H based on bond breaking vs bond making

required_transformations.description: Heating limestone to make quicklime -> CaCO3(s) -(Delta)-> CaO(s) + CO2(g)
Energy absorbed -> Decomposition reaction is endothermic (Delta H > 0)

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: If an equation is balanced, the reaction occurs spontaneously at room temperature
misconceptions.why_plausible: Paper chemistry does not display activation energy barriers
misconceptions.required_counterexample: H2 + O2 can sit mixed indefinitely at 25 deg C without reacting; a spark is required to overcome activation energy
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Explicitly mandate reaction condition annotations on every non-spontaneous transformation

problem_families.name: Reaction Condition and Thermochemical Classification
problem_families.recognition_cues: Reaction with temperature, catalyst, or Delta H indicators
problem_families.first_technical_move: Read arrow annotations and determine if reaction is exothermic or endothermic
problem_families.typical_unknown: Reaction type and required catalytic conditions

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Thermodynamic and kinetic condition requirements across reaction pathways

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Omitting required external conditions on non-spontaneous reactions
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Endothermic or catalytic reactions must declare required external conditions

subtopic_gates.chapter: Chemical Reactions and Equations / Chemical Foundations

provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 10 Science Chapter 1 & Johnstone Chemical Education Framework

technical_core.canonical_statement: Chemical understanding requires coherent translation across three levels: Macroscopic (tangible observations), Sub-microscopic / Particulate (atoms, molecules, ions), and Symbolic (formulas, equations, mathematics).
technical_core.why_required: Prevents rote symbolic formula manipulation disconnected from physical reality.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Learner manipulating equations without any mental model of reacting particles.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Every macroscopic observation (color change, temperature rise, precipitate, effervescence) must be causally linked to specific particulate species transformations.
technical_core.why_required: Ensures scientific causal attribution in chemical explanations.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Vague explanations attributing color change to 'the reaction' rather than specific product species.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: Shows direct binding between ionic species, formulas, and macroscopic visible phenomena

representations.name: Three-Level Chemistry Triplet Diagram
representations.chemistry_encoded: Three synchronized panels: Beaker photograph/sketch (Macroscopic), Ball-and-stick/particle model (Sub-microscopic), Chemical equation (Symbolic)
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Explicit bidirectional cross-reference links between particles and chemical formulas
representations.common_incorrect_version: Showing macroscopic beaker and equation but omitting particulate representation
representations.verification_method: Verify atom count in particulate model strictly matches coefficients in symbolic equation

model_conditions.why_needed: Atoms and molecules obey discrete counting
model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Continuous fluid mechanics assumptions blur chemical atomicity

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Record concrete macroscopic observation (e.g. effervescence, precipitate)
Map observation to chemical species formed (e.g. gas molecules, insoluble lattice)
Write balanced symbolic equation reflecting particulate transformation

required_transformations.description: Fizzes and bubbles -> Gas molecules dispersing from liquid
Counting 2 diatomic A2 and 1 diatomic B2 in box -> 2A2 + B2 -> 2A2B

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Individual sub-microscopic particles possess macroscopic properties (e.g. a sulfur atom is yellow, an atom of gold expands when heated)
misconceptions.why_plausible: Direct psychological projection of bulk sensory observations onto single atoms
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Color is an optical property of bulk electronic transitions; a single isolated atom has no bulk macroscopic color or melting point
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Strictly distinguish between emergent bulk macroscopic phenomena and single-particle quantum/atomic states

problem_families.name: Particulate-Box to Chemical Equation Translation
problem_families.recognition_cues: Diagram showing reacting particles in closed container before and after reaction
problem_families.first_technical_move: Count reactant molecules, identify excess species, and write stoichiometric ratio
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Including spectator or unreacted molecules as part of the core balanced equation
problem_families.typical_unknown: Balanced symbolic equation and limiting reactant

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Simultaneous coordination across sensory macroscopic, particulate sub-microscopic, and abstract symbolic representations

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Attributing macroscopic bulk properties to individual atoms
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Single atoms do not possess bulk macroscopic sensory properties

provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 9 Science Chapter 3, Section 3.5 (Mole Concept) & Grade 11 Chapter 1

technical_core.canonical_statement: One mole is the amount of substance containing exactly 6.02214076 x 10^23 elementary entities, with mass in grams numerically equal to relative formula mass.
technical_core.why_required: Connects microscopic particle counts directly to macroscopic weighable grams.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Inability to perform quantitative chemical calculations.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Stoichiometric coefficients define the exact molar ratios in which substances react and form, never direct mass ratios.
technical_core.why_required: Chemical reactions occur atom-for-atom and molecule-for-molecule, not gram-for-gram.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Equating coefficients directly to gram masses.

technical_core.canonical_statement: The limiting reagent is the reactant completely consumed first in a reaction, thereby capping the theoretical maximum yield of all products.
technical_core.why_required: Real reaction mixtures are rarely in exact stoichiometric balance.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Assuming all reactants are completely consumed regardless of initial quantities.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: n moles, m sample mass, M molar mass, N entity count, N_A Avogadro constant
mandatory_equations.conditions_of_validity: Pure chemical substance with known molecular formula

representations.name: Before-Change-After (BCA) Mole Table
representations.chemistry_encoded: Structured table tracking moles of all species before reaction, during change (-nu*x, +nu*x), and after completion
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Change line must strictly reflect stoichiometric coefficient ratios
representations.common_incorrect_version: Filling BCA table with gram masses instead of molar quantities
representations.verification_method: Check final moles >= 0 and limiting reagent final moles == 0

model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Incomplete reaction or equilibrium requires percent yield calculation

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Convert all given reactant masses or particle counts into moles (n = m/M)
Divide each reactant mole quantity by its stoichiometric coefficient to identify limiting reagent
Use limiting reactant moles to compute theoretical yield of products via molar ratio
Convert product moles back to requested units (grams or liters)

required_transformations.description: 36 g of H2O -> 36 / 18 = 2.0 mol H2O
2 mol H2 reacting with 1 mol O2 produces 2 mol H2O (36 g)

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Coefficients in an equation represent masses in grams (e.g. 2H2 + O2 -> 2H2O means 2g H2 reacts with 1g O2)
misconceptions.why_plausible: Confusing stoichiometric integer count with macroscopic gram weight
misconceptions.required_counterexample: 2 mol H2 has mass 4g; 1 mol O2 has mass 32g; they react in 4g : 32g (1:8 mass ratio), not 2:1
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Enforce mandatory conversion: mass -> moles -> mole ratio -> product mass

problem_families.name: Mass to Mole and Particle Interconversion
problem_families.recognition_cues: Given mass or number of molecules, calculate moles or atomic count
problem_families.first_technical_move: Compute molar mass from periodic table and apply n = m/M
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Using atomic mass instead of molecular mass for diatomic elements

problem_families.name: Limiting Reagent and Theoretical Yield Calculation
problem_families.recognition_cues: Given starting masses of two or more reactants
problem_families.first_technical_move: Convert all reactant masses to moles and compute n / nu for each
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Choosing limiting reactant by comparing masses directly without converting to moles
problem_families.typical_unknown: Limiting reactant and mass of product formed

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Multi-step quantitative dimensional analysis and limiting reactant branching logic

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Treating stoichiometric coefficients as gram mass ratios
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Stoichiometric coefficients dictate molar ratios, requiring molar mass conversion

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Acids, Bases, Aqueous Ionization & Net Ionic Neutralization

provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 10 Science Chapter 2 (Acids, Bases and Salts), Sections 2.1-2.3

technical_core.canonical_statement: Acids produce hydrogen/hydronium ions (H+ / H3O+) and bases produce hydroxide ions (OH-) exclusively in aqueous solution; moisture is mandatory for acidic/basic behavior.
technical_core.why_required: Explains why dry HCl gas or anhydrous citric acid fails to change dry litmus paper.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Believing acids act independently of water or solvent ionization.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Strong acids/bases dissociate completely in water (indicated by single arrow ->); weak acids/bases dissociate only partially, establishing dynamic equilibrium (indicated by double arrow <=>).
technical_core.why_required: Distinguishes concentration from acid strength.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Treating acetic acid dissociation as 100% complete.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Neutralization of a strong acid by a strong base is fundamentally the combination of H+(aq) and OH-(aq) to form liquid water, with spectator ions remaining dissolved.
technical_core.why_required: Reveals the true sub-microscopic chemical transformation behind acid-base reactions.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Viewing neutralization as a mysterious disappearance of acid rather than water formation.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: H+ aqueous hydronium/hydrogen ion, OH- aqueous hydroxide ion, H2O neutral liquid water
mandatory_equations.conditions_of_validity: Dilute aqueous solution at 25 deg C

representations.name: Hydronium Ion Solvation Model
representations.chemistry_encoded: Water molecule dipole orienting toward proton to form H3O+ ion in aqueous medium
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Explicit water molecule participation in proton hydration
representations.common_incorrect_version: Showing bare naked unhydrated protons floating in water
representations.verification_method: Check charge conservation across H+ + H2O -> H3O+

model_conditions.what_changes_if_violated: Neutral pH shifts from 7.0 at non-standard temperatures

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Identify acid/base species and presence of aqueous water solvent
Determine degree of ionization (complete -> vs partial <=>)
Write molecular equation, complete ionic equation, and cancel spectator ions for net ionic equation

required_transformations.description: HCl(aq) + NaOH(aq) -> NaCl(aq) + H2O(l) transformed to H+(aq) + OH-(aq) -> H2O(l)
Dry HCl gas does not turn dry litmus paper red because H+ ions are generated only in presence of water

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: Substances like dry HCl gas or solid citric acid crystals are acidic by themselves without water
misconceptions.why_plausible: They are named 'acids' on the reagent bottle
misconceptions.required_counterexample: Dry HCl gas passed over dry blue litmus paper shows zero color change; adding one drop of water instantly turns it red
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Enforce: acidic behavior is a property of hydrated H+(aq) / H3O+ ions formed upon aqueous dissolution

problem_families.name: Acid-Base Neutralization and Net Ionic Derivation
problem_families.recognition_cues: Reaction between acid and base forming salt and water
problem_families.first_technical_move: Split strong electrolytes into dissociated ions and identify non-participating spectator ions
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Splitting water or weak acids into separate free ions in complete ionic equation
problem_families.typical_unknown: Spectator ions and net ionic equation

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Ionization equilibrium distinctions and net ionic spectator cancellations

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Omitting the necessity of water for acid ionization
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Acidity requires aqueous dissociation into hydronium ions

subtopic_gates.learner_title: Redox Reactions, Oxidation States & Electron Transfer

provenance.source_reference: NCERT Grade 10 Science Chapter 1, Section 1.2.5 (Oxidation and Reduction)

technical_core.canonical_statement: Oxidation is the loss of electrons (increase in oxidation number); reduction is the gain of electrons (decrease in oxidation number); they occur simultaneously.
technical_core.why_required: Standard universal electron-transfer definition of redox.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Restricting redox solely to oxygen gain/loss.

technical_core.canonical_statement: Oxidation states are assigned by formal rules: free elements are 0, monoatomic ions equal their charge, oxygen is -2 (except peroxides), hydrogen is +1 (with nonmetals), and the sum equals the overall species charge.
technical_core.why_required: Enforces rigorous bookkeeping of electron transfer.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Arbitrary assignment of oxidation numbers.

technical_core.canonical_statement: The oxidizing agent is the reactant species that causes oxidation by accepting electrons (and is itself reduced); the reducing agent donates electrons (and is itself oxidized).
technical_core.why_required: Agent role terminology is systematically inverted relative to the substance oxidized/reduced.
technical_core.failure_if_omitted: Claiming the substance oxidized is the oxidizing agent.

mandatory_equations.meaning_of_symbols: CuO copper(II) oxide (Cu reduced from +2 to 0, oxidizing agent), H2 hydrogen gas (H oxidized from 0 to +1, reducing agent)

representations.name: Redox Oxidation Number Tracking Arc Diagram
representations.chemistry_encoded: Balanced equation with oxidation numbers written above elements, connected by bridging arcs labeled 'Oxidation (loss of e-)' and 'Reduction (gain of e-)'
representations.what_cannot_be_omitted: Explicit numerical tracking of electron gain and loss confirming equal exchange
representations.common_incorrect_version: Drawing arrows without specifying electron transfer numbers
representations.verification_method: Check total electrons lost by reducing agent equals total electrons gained by oxidizing agent

model_conditions.why_needed: Free electrons cannot accumulate in bulk chemical media

reasoning_sequence.expert_action: Assign oxidation numbers to every atom on reactant and product sides
Identify species whose oxidation number increased (oxidized) and decreased (reduced)
Apply agent inversion rule to designate oxidizing and reducing agents
Verify electron loss equals electron gain across balanced half-reactions

required_transformations.description: Zn + CuSO4 -> ZnSO4 + Cu -> Zn is oxidized (reducing agent), Cu^2+ is reduced (oxidizing agent)
Combine Fe^2+ -> Fe^3+ + e- and MnO4^- + 8H+ + 5e- -> Mn^2+ + 4H2O by multiplying by 5

misconceptions.incorrect_belief: The oxidizing agent is the substance that gets oxidized
misconceptions.why_plausible: Confusing the agent causing the action with the recipient of the action
misconceptions.required_counterexample: A travel agent sends others on travel; an oxidizing agent oxidizes another substance by taking its electrons, and is therefore reduced itself
misconceptions.required_technical_repair: Enforce: Oxidizing agent = species reduced (electron acceptor); Reducing agent = species oxidized (electron donor)

problem_families.name: Redox Identification and Agent Assignment
problem_families.recognition_cues: Chemical equation with potential change in oxidation numbers or electron transfer
problem_families.first_technical_move: Assign oxidation states to all atoms before and after arrow
problem_families.common_fatal_error: Classifying the substance oxidized as the oxidizing agent
problem_families.typical_unknown: Substance oxidized, substance reduced, oxidizing agent, reducing agent

difficulty_profile.difficulty_basis: Complex simultaneous electron bookkeeping and linguistic role inversion

falsification_cases.authoring_defect: Conflating oxidizing agent with oxidized species
falsification_cases.expected_failure_reason: Oxidizing agent causes oxidation and is itself reduced
